Settings
Character
SetupWalks through setup again with your current info filled in. Nothing is erased: only what you change is saved.
Auto-refreshPull your stats from the hiscores every 15 minutes.
Fill in Scroll from your statsDays you never logged by hand still show the XP the hiscores saw.
RuneLite data
Pages
TabsWhat Scroll, Achievements, Quest Hub, Coffer, Skills and Upgrades open on when you come back to them. The app itself always opens on Home.
NumbersHow skill XP is shown.
Look
LayoutHow Home's panes are arranged. Mosaic is uneven on purpose, and you can drag a pane by its header to move it. Orderly lines every edge up.
Command lineThe line at the top of every page takes commands: cd scroll, log mined for an hour, stats mining, -help for the list. Press / or the key under Esc to start typing. On a wide window the console sits in its own column at the right of every page; the console button on the line shows and hides it, and dragging its header off floats it over the page. Off leaves the line as a plain path.
ConsoleWhere the console sits. At the side is a column to the right of every page, when the window has room. Floating is a window you can move and resize. Hidden closes it. The shortcut shows and hides it from anywhere; drag the console's header to pull it off the side.
Bakery layoutHow Coffer's Bakery is laid out. Board puts the best three side by side and the rest in tiles. Listing is one aligned table with the row you choose opened beside it. The same switch is on the page itself.
Progress barsHow a bar is drawn, everywhere one appears: under a skill, beside a day, on a goal.
BackdropWhat sits behind the panes. Clean is no pattern, with a soft glow in the corners. Dots, Grid, Lines and Weave are faint patterns. Flat is the theme's plain colour.
Wide windowOn a wide monitor, the room beside and under a page fills with extra panes. The most useful come first, so more room only ever adds less essential ones. A pane's x hides it.
Theme
Scene artThe picture a theme carries. Focused shows a little of it, Illustrated shows more, Off shows none.
Font

Headings and numbers throughout the app. Body text stays as it is.

The Terminal look sets its own type. These apply when the look is Classic.

Priorities touched
editing

Log

Priorities

The things you do not want to slack on. Give each a weekly target and it counts itself from your experience and kills. Tag a journal entry or press ✓ for what the hiscores cannot see.

Ideas: what people focus on

Drawn from community guides to account progress and daily routines. Press one to add it with a starting weekly target, then change the target or park it on its own row.

➕ Add a priority

Track via: Skill and Boss count themselves from your experience and kills. Activity is a hiscores score, such as clue scrolls. Journal tag counts any day your journal carries that tag, such as Questing. Manual counts only when you press its tick.

📊 Recap

🗺️ Roadmap

The long arc — the unlocks, gear, and milestones your account is headed toward. Level-gated things tick themselves from your stats; quests and drops you tick when they happen.

🔥 In reach

The locked things you're closest to — computed from your live stats.

💬 Wise Old Bud

The Wise Old Man's less accomplished cousin. Checks requirements against your live stats.
Library currently covers the big bosses, unlock quests, and common gear — it's growing. Try: can I do Barrows yet? · what do I need for Vorkath? · can I wear a whip?

Every skill, where you are in it, and the wiki's guide for the stretch ahead. Tap a skill.

🎯 Goals & to-dos

Setting goals in OSRS matters — it gives you something to look forward to and keeps you moving in a productive direction. The world is a massive sandbox; move through it however you see fit.

Tip: after adding one, use + Step on it to break it into checkable steps.
